title: Christ Our Mediator
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Christ our Mediator means that Jesus alone brings God and sinners together through His person and work. He is the one Mediator who represents God to humanity and humanity before God.
summary: Christ our Mediator means that Jesus alone brings God and sinners together through His person and work. He is the one Mediator who represents God to humanity and humanity before God.
christFocus: Jesus is the Mediator because He is truly God and truly man. Through His blood, priesthood, and covenant work, He reconciles sinners to God and gives them access to the Father.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Sin separates people from God, and sinners cannot bridge that separation by themselves. They need a Mediator appointed by God who can bring them near.

Jesus is uniquely qualified because He is both God and man. He reveals God perfectly, represents humanity truly, and gives Himself as the ransom for sinners.

His mediation is covenantal and saving. Through His death, He secures redemption and brings His people into the blessings of the new covenant.

There is one Mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus. No priest, saint, angel, religious system, or personal effort can replace His mediating work.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People often try to approach God through their own sincerity, religious performance, spiritual experiences, or human mediators. Scripture points to Christ alone.

This doctrine gives peace to those who feel far from God. Access to the Father is not earned by emotional strength or religious status, but given through Jesus the Mediator.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Come to God through Christ alone. Do not trust your worthiness, another human mediator, or religious effort to bring you near. Pray, worship, repent, and hope through the One who has opened the way to the Father.
